claims.text: THE LAKEBED HAS BEEN PHOTOGRAPHED FROM THE AIR, LEGALLY, AND THERE IS NOTHING ON IT. Tyler Rogoway of The War Zone published aerial images taken on a pilot's authorised flight directly over Papoose Lake: 'nothing appears to be there, just as satellite images show. There isn't even an access road and, as you can see, the lakebed is flooded, which is a fairly common occurrence.' Rogoway states his own position in the same piece: 'No, I don't believe Bob's story, but I do think that it is one of the most entertaining tales ever told.'

claims.text: THE SECOND-BEST FINDING IN THIS CLUSTER: TWO PEOPLE REACH THE SAME COUNTER-EXPLANATION BY UNRELATED ROUTES. Tom Mahood, a physics graduate who spent years on the documentary record, concludes in his 2018 retrospective that there is 'nothing at Papoose Lake' and that S-4 actually refers to a radar facility at the Tonopah Test Range. Separately, T.D. Barnes, a former CIA and NASA engineer who worked at Groom Lake, says the real Site 4 is a remote radar site north of the main facility that held captured Soviet equipment, that this and not an underground base is what Lazar referred to, and that a named retired Area 51 security chief confirmed to him that Lazar appears on no manifest. Neither route depends on the other: one is documentary and civilian, the other is recollection by a former range engineer. Shared conclusions from a shared method are not corroboration; these two do not share a method.

claims.text: THE CLAIM'S GEOGRAPHY MOVED, ON THE CONTEMPORANEOUS RECORD. The Las Vegas Review-Journal of 21 August 1990 describes Lazar's claim, as of that date, as being that 'the U.S. government was testing alien spacecraft at the Nevada Test Site, 65 miles northwest of Las Vegas'. That is a different named place from Papoose Lake and from the Nellis range. The board carries the discrepancy on the hub rather than smoothing it into the later settled version.

NEGATIVE FINDING, STATED AS ONE. No opened government record of any kind names a facility called S-4 at Papoose Lake. That is a statement about the searching done on 18 September 2026 and it is not a proof of absence.

desc: THIS NODE RECORDS A CLAIM AND NOT A PLACE WHOSE CONTENTS ARE ESTABLISHED. Papoose Lake is a real dry lake bed in Lincoln County, Nevada, a few miles southwest of the Groom Lake facility and adjacent to the Papoose Range. Nothing documented attaches any facility to it. What attaches to it is an assertion: from 1989 Bob Lazar has said that between December 1988 and April 1989 he worked at a site he calls S-4, about fifteen miles south of Groom Lake on the Nellis range, built into a mountainside behind nine hangar doors angled at about sixty degrees, holding nine disc-shaped craft whose propulsion he was hired to back-engineer. The node exists because that assertion is the convergence point of an entire cluster: Lazar, John Lear, Gene Huff, George Knapp, the 1989 KLAS broadcasts, the 1991 videotape and the 2018 Corbell documentary all run into it, and so do the people who say it is wrong. The documented half of the surrounding geography is real and should not be blurred into the claim: the Groom Lake facility was officially acknowledged when the CIA history of the U-2 and OXCART programmes by Gregory Pedlow and Donald Welzenbach was declassified in summer 2013. That is a statement about Groom Lake. It is not a statement about Papoose Lake. The node is named s-4-papoose-lake rather than s-4 deliberately, because the two strongest sceptical accounts both say the designator S-4 is real and attaches to a radar facility elsewhere on the range; a node called s-4 would silently adopt the claimant's referent as the board's own.
label: S-4 / Papoose Lake, Nevada
